subject: general
question: Name the caves found in western India on the Island of Gharapuris which received the UNESCO heritage site status in 1987.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Elephanta Caves**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Elephanta Caves **was declared a **UNESCO World Heritage Site **in 1987 after being repaired.
 
• **The Archaeological Survey of India(ASI)** currently looks after the Elephanta Caves. They are a series of cave temples mostly dedicated to the Hindu god Shiva. They have been designated as a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
 
• The Elephanta Caves feature rock-cut stone sculptures, most of which are in high relief, that demonstrate a synthesis of Hindu and Buddhist concepts and imagery.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__** 

 
• The **Ajanta Caves** are approximately 30 rock-cut Buddhist cave monuments dating from the 2nd century BCE to about 480 CE in the Aurangabad district of Maharashtra state in India.
 
• **Ellora **is a **UNESCO World Heritage Site **located in the **Aurangabad **district of Maharashtra, India. It is one of the largest rock-cut Hindu temple cave complexes in the world, with artwork dating from the period 600–1000 CE.
 
• **Elephanta Island** is one of several islands in Mumbai Harbour, located east of the city.
 
• The **Nandi** **temple **is a Hindu temple located in **Khajuraho **city of Madhya Pradesh, India. It is dedicated to Nandi, the bull which serves as the mount of Shiva, in Hindu epic. As a common architecture trend, temples of Shiva display stone images of a seated Nandi facing Shiva.
